Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Give each of finitely many bundles $E_j$ a connection. Use the tensor bundle constructed in [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]], including its multilinear model on the dual fibres. The **product connection** is characterized on local elementary tensors by
$$\nabla_X(s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes s_k)=\sum_j s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\nabla^j_Xs_j\otimes\cdots\otimes s_k.$$
For the empty product, the connection on scalar functions is $\nabla_Xf=X(f)$.

To construct it without a decomposition assumption, for a multilinear-model section $T$ and local dual sections $\alpha_j$ put
$$(\nabla_XT)(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)=X\bigl(T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)\bigr)-\sum_jT(\alpha_1,\ldots,(\nabla^j)^*_X\alpha_j,\ldots,\alpha_k).$$
Use the dual connections of [[def-dual-connection]]. Multiplying any argument by a smooth $f$ produces two opposite $X(f)T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)$ terms; thus this expression is function-linear in every dual argument. In dual frames its coefficients are smooth and depend only on their fibre values, so it defines a smooth tensor section. The same intrinsic expression on overlaps gives agreement. Its real-linearity, function-linearity in $X$, and rule $\nabla_X(fT)=X(f)T+f\nabla_XT$ follow by direct expansion, establishing the connection. This also gives the gluing criterion of [[thm-local-connection-forms-glue-exactly-when-they-obey-the-transformation-law]].

On a pure tensor, the scalar product rule and the dual pairing identity reduce this expression to the first displayed sum. Hence it respects the balanced identity $(fs)\otimes t=s\otimes(ft)$: either derivative gives the same term $X(f)s\otimes t$ and the same two terms multiplied by $f$. Every section has a finite local product-frame expansion, so that rule and the connection Leibniz identity force uniqueness.

For bundles $E,F$, identify $F\otimes E^*$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)$ by $t\otimes\alpha\mapsto(v\mapsto\alpha(v)t)$. In local bases these elementary tensors are precisely the matrix units, proving this is a smooth fibrewise isomorphism. The induced **Hom connection** is therefore
$$(\nabla_XA)(s)=\nabla^F_X(A(s))-A(\nabla^E_Xs).$$
The two $X(f)A(s)$ terms cancel when $s$ is replaced by $fs$, ensuring a fibrewise map. Rank-zero factors give zero bundles, whereas the empty product is the scalar line; these conventions are different. No choice beyond finitely many local frames is needed.

For $a>0$, the function $x\mapsto a^x$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$ and
$$(a^x)'=a^x\log a.$$
For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ is continuous and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, with
$$(x^\alpha)'=\alpha x^{\alpha-1}.$$

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $k\in\mathbb N$. Finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps is $C^k$. Scalar multiples are included among the finite componentwise operations. The assertions remain valid on an empty open domain.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Give each of finitely many bundles $E_j$ a connection. Use the tensor bundle constructed in [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]], including its multilinear model on the dual fibres. The **product connection** is characterized on local elementary tensors by
$$\nabla_X(s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes s_k)=\sum_j s_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\nabla^j_Xs_j\otimes\cdots\otimes s_k.$$
For the empty product, the connection on scalar functions is $\nabla_Xf=X(f)$.

To construct it without a decomposition assumption, for a multilinear-model section $T$ and local dual sections $\alpha_j$ put
$$(\nabla_XT)(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)=X\bigl(T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)\bigr)-\sum_jT(\alpha_1,\ldots,(\nabla^j)^*_X\alpha_j,\ldots,\alpha_k).$$
Use the dual connections of [[def-dual-connection]]. Multiplying any argument by a smooth $f$ produces two opposite $X(f)T(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)$ terms; thus this expression is function-linear in every dual argument. In dual frames its coefficients are smooth and depend only on their fibre values, so it defines a smooth tensor section. The same intrinsic expression on overlaps gives agreement. Its real-linearity, function-linearity in $X$, and rule $\nabla_X(fT)=X(f)T+f\nabla_XT$ follow by direct expansion, establishing the connection. This also gives the gluing criterion of [[thm-local-connection-forms-glue-exactly-when-they-obey-the-transformation-law]].

On a pure tensor, the scalar product rule and the dual pairing identity reduce this expression to the first displayed sum. Hence it respects the balanced identity $(fs)\otimes t=s\otimes(ft)$: either derivative gives the same term $X(f)s\otimes t$ and the same two terms multiplied by $f$. Every section has a finite local product-frame expansion, so that rule and the connection Leibniz identity force uniqueness.

For bundles $E,F$, identify $F\otimes E^*$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(E,F)$ by $t\otimes\alpha\mapsto(v\mapsto\alpha(v)t)$. In local bases these elementary tensors are precisely the matrix units, proving this is a smooth fibrewise isomorphism. The induced **Hom connection** is therefore
$$(\nabla_XA)(s)=\nabla^F_X(A(s))-A(\nabla^E_Xs).$$
The two $X(f)A(s)$ terms cancel when $s$ is replaced by $fs$, ensuring a fibrewise map. Rank-zero factors give zero bundles, whereas the empty product is the scalar line; these conventions are different. No choice beyond finitely many local frames is needed.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, metric $g$, and future cone of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Here timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, null means $v\ne0$ and $g(v,v)=0$, causal means timelike or null, and a nonzero causal vector is future-directed when $g(v,N)<0$, as in that supplier. A future unit observer is a vector $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$. At a point $p$, let $T_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous real symmetric bilinear form, represented by the covariant tensor $T_{ab}$. Define its metric trace by $\operatorname{tr}_g T:=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ and its raised mixed tensor by $T^a{}_b:=g^{ac}T_{cb}$.

- The **weak energy condition (WEC)** holds at $p$ when $T_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v\in T_pM$.
- The **null energy condition (NEC)** holds at $p$ when $T_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future-directed null $\ell\in T_pM$.
- The **strong energy condition (SEC)** holds at $p$ when the WEC holds for the trace-reversed tensor $T_{ab}-\tfrac12(\operatorname{tr}_gT)g_{ab}$.
- The **dominant energy condition (DEC)** holds at $p$ when, for every future-directed timelike $v\in T_pM$, the vector $J^a:=-T^a{}_bv^b$ is future causal or zero.

These are pointwise algebraic conditions. They are independent of an Einstein equation or an assertion that a physical material realizes $T$. The continuous regularity suffices for the definitions; any differentiability needed for a conservation identity is a separate hypothesis.

For a future unit observer $n$, observer energy density means $T_{ab}n^an^b$. The observer energy-current vector is $-T^a{}_bn^b$, and its spatial energy flux is the projection of this vector into the positive rest space $n^\perp$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

derivations.claim: In a positively oriented orthonormal frame with future unit time vector $n=e_0$, the convention in [F1] gives $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, and $F_{ab}F^{ab}=2(|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2)$. Substitution in the tensor formula yields $T^{00}_{\mathrm{EM}}=u$ and $T^{0i}_{\mathrm{EM}}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_jB_k/(\mu_0c)$. Symmetry follows because $g_{cd}F^{ac}F^{bd}$ is symmetric in $a,b$; its trace is $\mu_0^{-1}(F_{cd}F^{cd}-\tfrac14\cdot4F_{cd}F^{cd})=0$.

In a fluid rest frame $T^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(\epsilon,p,p,p)$. For a future timelike vector $v=(v^0,\mathbf v)$, $v^0>|\mathbf v|$, its quadratic form is $T(v,v)=\epsilon((v^0)^2-|\mathbf v|^2)+(\epsilon+p)|\mathbf v|^2$. Thus $\epsilon\ge0$ and $\epsilon+p\ge0$ suffice for WEC; past timelike vectors give the same value as their negatives. Necessity follows by taking $v=(1,0,0,0)$, which forces $\epsilon\ge0$, and then $v=(1,r,0,0)$ with $r\uparrow1$: if $\epsilon+p<0$, the displayed value tends to that negative number, so is negative for some $r<1$. For a nonzero future null $\ell$, $T(\ell,\ell)=(\epsilon+p)|\boldsymbol\ell|^2$, so NEC is equivalent to $\epsilon+p\ge0$.

The mixed tensor of the perfect fluid is $T^a{}_b=\operatorname{diag}(-\epsilon,p,p,p)$ in the same frame. Hence $-T^a{}_bv^b=(\epsilon v^0,-p\mathbf v)$. If $\epsilon\ge|p|$, then its time component is nonnegative and its squared norm is $-\epsilon^2(v^0)^2+p^2|\mathbf v|^2\le-\epsilon^2((v^0)^2-|\mathbf v|^2)\le0$; it is therefore future causal or zero for every $v^0>|\mathbf v|$. Conversely the rest vector forces $\epsilon\ge0$, while requiring the vector to be causal for $(1,r,0,0)$ gives $\epsilon^2-p^2r^2\ge0$ for every $0<r<1$. Letting $r\uparrow1$ yields $\epsilon\ge|p|$. This proves DEC iff $\epsilon\ge|p|$.

Put $a=E/c$ and $b=B$. For any future unit observer used as the time vector of such a frame, the observer energy current $-T^a{}_bn^b$ has components $(u,(a\times b)/\mu_0)$. The component identity $|a\times b|^2=|a|^2|b|^2-(a\cdot b)^2$ and $(|a|-|b|)^2\ge0$ give $|a\times b|/\mu_0\le |a||b|/\mu_0\le (|a|^2+|b|^2)/(2\mu_0)=u$. Its time component is nonnegative and its squared norm is $-u^2+|a\times b|^2/\mu_0^2\le0$, so it is future causal or zero for every future unit observer. Every future timelike $v$ is a positive multiple of a future unit vector; the current scales by that same positive factor, proving DEC for all such $v$.

The trace is $-\epsilon+3p$. The trace-reversed tensor $T_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}T_{cd})g_{ab}$ has rest energy density $(\epsilon+3p)/2$ and pressure $(\epsilon-p)/2$. Applying the WEC equivalence from step 1.2 to this tensor gives SEC iff $\epsilon+3p\ge0$ and $\epsilon+p\ge0$.

For a future timelike $v$, DEC gives a future-causal $J^a=-T^a{}_bv^b$. In the rest frame of $v$, $v=(v^0,0,0,0)$ with $v^0>0$ and $J^0\ge0$, so $T_{ab}v^av^b=-g(J,v)=v^0J^0\ge0$; this proves WEC for future timelike vectors, and $T(-v,-v)=T(v,v)$ proves it for past timelike vectors too. For a nonzero future null $\ell$, vectors $\ell+\delta n$ are future timelike for every $\delta>0$ and tend to $\ell$, so continuity of the quadratic form proves NEC. Since $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ has zero trace by step 1.1, its trace-reversed tensor equals itself; SEC is therefore WEC.
For dust, write $\epsilon=\rho c^2$ and $p=0$; then $T_m^{ab}=\epsilon U^aU^b/c^2$ is the perfect-fluid tensor. Steps 1.2–3.1 give all four conditions because $\rho\ge0$.

For a finite family, the future causal cone in an orthonormal frame consists of $(t,\mathbf x)$ with $t\ge|\mathbf x|$. If $J_i=(t_i,\mathbf x_i)$ lie in this cone, then $\sum_i t_i\ge\sum_i|\mathbf x_i|\ge|\sum_i\mathbf x_i|$, so their sum is future causal. Since the DEC current is linear in $T$, finite sums preserve DEC. The WEC and NEC inequalities are linear in $T$, and trace reversal is linear in $T$, so finite sums preserve WEC, NEC and SEC as well. Therefore the Maxwell and nonnegative-dust conclusions add. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with an affine connection $\nabla$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be any interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]), and let $z:I\to M$ be continuous. We say that $z$ is **$C^2$ on $I$** in this definition when the following chartwise conditions hold. At each interior parameter value $\tau_0\in\operatorname{int}I$, there are a chart $x:U\to x(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ around $z(\tau_0)$ and an open interval $J\subseteq\operatorname{int}I$ containing $\tau_0$, with $z(J)\subseteq U$, such that $x\circ z$ is twice continuously differentiable on $J$. At each included endpoint $\tau_0\in I\setminus\operatorname{int}I$, there are such a chart and a relative neighborhood $J=I\cap(\tau_0-\delta,\tau_0+\delta)$, with $\delta>0$ and $z(J)\subseteq U$, for which the first and second derivatives on $J\cap\operatorname{int}I$ extend continuously to $\tau_0$; their endpoint values are the corresponding one-sided derivatives. Here $n=\dim M$, and differentiability of $x\circ z$ is componentwise as a map of one real variable. Smooth chart transitions and $C^2$ composition make this condition independent of the chosen chart ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]); at an included endpoint, the first- and second-derivative chain-rule expressions have the corresponding continuous one-sided limits. On a time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, this is exactly the curve regularity specified in clause (a) of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]; that definition's causal conditions are not part of the present regularity convention.

The parameter $\tau$ is an arbitrary real parameter here; no causal or nonzero-velocity condition is imposed. Put $U(\tau):=z'(\tau)$, using the one-sided derivative at included endpoints. A **vector field along $z$** assigns $V(\tau)\in T_{z(\tau)}M$ to each $\tau\in I$; it is **continuous** when its component functions are continuous in every chart along $z$. In a chart $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$ covering a segment of $z$, write $U^a(\tau):=\frac{d}{d\tau}(x^a\circ z)(\tau)$ and let $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$. The components $U^a$ transform by the tangent-map Jacobian on chart overlaps, by the chain rule, so $U$ is a vector field along $z$. All indices range from $1$ to $n$, and repeated upper/lower indices are summed. Define the **covariant acceleration of $z$** on this segment by the component formula

$$\bigl(\nabla_UU\bigr)^a(\tau):=\frac{dU^a}{d\tau}(\tau)+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(z(\tau))U^b(\tau)U^c(\tau).$$

The local $C^2$ regularity makes $U^a$ continuously differentiable, including one-sided endpoint derivatives, so these components are continuous on the relative parameter interval. The name and notation extend the pullback covariant derivative of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] from smooth curves; the coordinate expression is well-defined on overlaps by [[lem-emg-c2-curve-covariant-acceleration-well-defined]].

Let $e=(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ be a local frame of $E$ on an open set $U$, in the sense of [[def-local-frame-and-global-frame-of-a-vector-bundle]]. Restrict a given connection to $U$ by [[lem-a-bundle-connection-is-local-and-restricts-to-open-sets]]. Its **connection one-form in the frame $e$** is the matrix $\omega=(\omega^i{}_j)$ of scalar one-forms on $U$ characterized by
$$\nabla_X e_j=\sum_i\omega^i{}_j(X)e_i.$$
For each $j$, the smooth Hom section $\nabla e_j$ has unique fibre coordinates in $e$; these coordinates are linear in the direction and smooth, hence are scalar one-forms. Smoothness may be tested in any coordinate chart and frame, using [[prop-smoothness-of-a-section-is-equivalent-to-smooth-local-components]].

Our convention treats $e$ as a row and the coefficients $u$ of $s=eu$ as a column. A frame change is $e'=eA$ with a smooth invertible matrix $A$, so $u=Au'$ for the same section. Products of matrices and one-forms use ordinary matrix multiplication with scalar functions as coefficients. In a coordinate chart, $\omega^i{}_j=\sum_k\Gamma^i{}_{kj}\,dx^k$; this notation does not assert tensorial transformation for $\Gamma$.

For rank zero the frame and connection matrix are empty; for rank one $\omega$ is a scalar one-form. On a zero-dimensional base every one-form is zero. The frame is supplied locally, so this definition involves no global selection or existence theorem.

For an affine connection as in [[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]] and coordinates $(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$, its **Christoffel symbols** in this chart are the unique smooth functions $\Gamma^k{}_{ij}$ such that
$$\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\sum_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\partial_k.$$
The first lower index $i$ is the differentiating direction and the second lower index $j$ labels the differentiated vector field. In the coordinate frame, the one-forms from [[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]] are $\omega^k{}_j=\sum_i\Gamma^k{}_{ij}\,dx^i$. A different chart generally has different symbols. This definition asserts neither symmetry in $i,j$ nor tensorial transformation.

For dimension one there is one smooth coefficient $\Gamma^1{}_{11}$; in dimension zero there are no coefficients. All statements are local, and at a boundary chart the derivatives are the smooth up-to-boundary coordinate derivatives.

If $e'=eA$ are two frames on an overlap, their matrices for the same connection satisfy
$$\omega'=A^{-1}\omega A+A^{-1}dA.$$
All entries of $dA$ are differentials of scalar functions; the order of the matrix factors is as displayed.

Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth manifolds, let $F:M\to N$ be a map, let $p\in M$ and
let $r\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$, where $\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$.
For $m,q\in\mathbb N_0$ and an open set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, a map
$g:E\to\mathbb R^q$ is **of class $C^r$** as follows. When $m=0$, every such
map is declared $C^r$. When $m\ge1$, each component $g_l$ with $l<q$ must be
$C^r$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]; when $q=0$ this
component condition is vacuous.
Suppose $F$ is continuous at $p$. Then $F$ is **of class $C^r$ at $p$** when
there are smooth charts $(U,\varphi)$ of $M$ at $p$ and $(V,\psi)$ of $N$ at
$F(p)$ with $F(U)\subseteq V$ such that the coordinate representative

$$\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\longrightarrow\psi(V)$$

([[def-coordinate-representation-of-a-map]]) is of class $C^r$ on a
neighbourhood of $\varphi(p)$ in this componentwise Euclidean sense. By
[[lem-chart-independence-of-c-r-smoothness]], this condition is independent of
the chosen charts: if one such representative is $C^r$, then every one is, so
"some charts" may be read as "any charts". A map is **$C^r$ on an open set**
$W\subseteq M$ when it is continuous on $W$ and $C^r$ at every point of $W$. A
map that is $C^r$ for every finite $r$ — equivalently $C^\infty$ — is called
**smooth**; the term **$C^r$ map between smooth manifolds** is reserved for the
case where $F$ is continuous and the representative condition holds at every
point of $M$.

Let $k\in\mathbb N$. Finite componentwise sums and products of $C^k$ Euclidean maps are $C^k$, and a composite of composable $C^k$ Euclidean maps is $C^k$. Scalar multiples are included among the finite componentwise operations. The assertions remain valid on an empty open domain.

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-ordered-field]]) with its order
([[def-real-order]]).

A subset $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is **order-convex** when

$$x, y \in I \text{ and } x \le z \le y \;\Longrightarrow\; z \in I .$$

The **intervals** of $\mathbb{R}$ are the sets of the following nine forms, where
$a, b \in \mathbb{R}$:

| | bounded forms | | one-sided and full forms |
|---|---|---|---|
| $(a,b)$ | $\{x : a < x < b\}$ | $(a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a < x\}$ |
| $[a,b]$ | $\{x : a \le x \le b\}$ | $[a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a \le x\}$ |
| $[a,b)$ | $\{x : a \le x < b\}$ | $(-\infty,b)$ | $\{x : x < b\}$ |
| $(a,b]$ | $\{x : a < x \le b\}$ | $(-\infty,b]$ | $\{x : x \le b\}$ |
| | | $(-\infty,\infty)$ | $\mathbb{R}$ |

An interval is **open** when both of its written endpoints are excluded, that is
for the forms $(a,b)$, $(a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b)$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$; it is
**closed** when both written endpoints are included, that is for $[a,b]$,
$[a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b]$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$. The forms $[a,b)$ and
$(a,b]$ are **half-open**.

**The symbols $\pm\infty$ are notation and not elements of $\mathbb{R}$.** They
mark which side carries no endpoint condition at all; the five forms in the right
column are defined by the displayed conditions on $x$ alone, and no arithmetic is
ever performed with $\infty$. This is the same refusal to extend $\mathbb{R}$
silently that [[rem-sup-conventions]] records for suprema.

**Every one of the nine forms is order-convex.** Each is defined by a conjunction
of at most two conditions, each of the shape $a < x$, $a \le x$, $x < b$ or
$x \le b$, and each such condition is inherited by an intermediate point: if
$a < x$ and $x \le z$ then $a < z$, and if $z \le y$ and $y < b$ then $z < b$,
by transitivity of the order ([[def-ordered-field]]). Applying this to whichever
one or two conditions define the form in question gives $z \in I$ whenever
$x, y \in I$ and $x \le z \le y$.

**Bounded intervals.** An interval is **bounded** ([[def-bounded-set]]) exactly
when it is of one of the four forms in the left column: for those, $a$ is a lower
bound and $b$ an upper bound. The other five forms are unbounded, on the side or
sides written with $\infty$; the verification is in the remarks below.

**Nondegeneracy.** An interval is **degenerate** when it has at most one element,
and **nondegenerate** when it has at least two. For the four bounded forms with
endpoints $a$ and $b$:

- $[a,b]$ is nonempty exactly when $a \le b$, and it is nondegenerate exactly
  when $a < b$. It is the singleton $\{a\}$ when $a = b$.
- $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are nonempty exactly when $a < b$, and then each
  is nondegenerate.

The only assertion here that is not immediate from the defining conditions is
that $a < b$ makes $(a,b)$ nonempty with at least two points. It holds because
$a < (a+b)/2 < b$, which follows from $a < b$ by adding $a$, respectively $b$, to
both sides and halving ([[def-ordered-field]]); repeating the halving inside
$(a, (a+b)/2)$ produces a second point.

**Closed bounded intervals.** These are the sets $[a,b]$ with $a \le b$, which is
exactly the condition making them nonempty. They are the intervals the nested
interval property is stated for, and the phrase *closed bounded interval* always
carries the hypothesis $a \le b$ in this library.

**Length.** The **length** of a bounded interval presented by its endpoints
$a \le b$ is

$$\ell = b - a \;\ge\; 0 .$$

Length is attached to the presentation by endpoints and is not recovered from the
set: $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are all empty when $a = b$, and so is
$(c,c)$ for any other $c$, while each of these presentations has length $0$, so
nothing inconsistent arises; but the endpoints are named explicitly at every
point where a length is used in this library, and never inferred from the set.
Unbounded intervals are assigned no length.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with an affine connection $\nabla$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be any interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]), and let $z:I\to M$ be continuous. We say that $z$ is **$C^2$ on $I$** in this definition when the following chartwise conditions hold. At each interior parameter value $\tau_0\in\operatorname{int}I$, there are a chart $x:U\to x(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ around $z(\tau_0)$ and an open interval $J\subseteq\operatorname{int}I$ containing $\tau_0$, with $z(J)\subseteq U$, such that $x\circ z$ is twice continuously differentiable on $J$. At each included endpoint $\tau_0\in I\setminus\operatorname{int}I$, there are such a chart and a relative neighborhood $J=I\cap(\tau_0-\delta,\tau_0+\delta)$, with $\delta>0$ and $z(J)\subseteq U$, for which the first and second derivatives on $J\cap\operatorname{int}I$ extend continuously to $\tau_0$; their endpoint values are the corresponding one-sided derivatives. Here $n=\dim M$, and differentiability of $x\circ z$ is componentwise as a map of one real variable. Smooth chart transitions and $C^2$ composition make this condition independent of the chosen chart ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]); at an included endpoint, the first- and second-derivative chain-rule expressions have the corresponding continuous one-sided limits. On a time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, this is exactly the curve regularity specified in clause (a) of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]; that definition's causal conditions are not part of the present regularity convention.

derivations.claim: In an $x$-chart, $U_x(\tau)$ is $C^1$ in the interior and its derivative extends continuously to each included endpoint by [F5]. The connection coefficients composed with $z$ and $U_x$ are continuous, so $a_x=\dot U_x+\omega_x(\dot z_x)U_x$ is continuous on the relative parameter segment, using one-sided endpoint values.

On an overlap with coordinates $y$, put $J(\tau):=\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}(z(\tau))$ and $A(\tau):=J(\tau)^{-1}$, so the coordinate frames satisfy $e_y=e_xA$ and $U_y=JU_x$. By [F3], $\omega_y(\dot z_y)=J\omega_x(\dot z_x)A+J\dot A$. Differentiating $AJ=I$ gives $\dot A J+A\dot J=0$, hence $J\dot A J=-\dot J$. Differentiating $U_y=JU_x$ and using this identity gives $\dot U_y+\omega_y(\dot z_y)U_y=\dot J U_x+J\dot U_x+J\omega_x(\dot z_x)U_x+J\dot A J U_x=J(\dot U_x+\omega_x(\dot z_x)U_x)$ at every interior parameter value. Both sides extend continuously to included endpoints by [F4] and [F5], so the equality holds there by taking the one-sided limit. Thus the candidate components transform by the tangent-vector Jacobian. They agree as vectors on every overlap; the locally defined continuous fields therefore patch uniquely to a continuous vector field along $z$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra] ∎

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

Let $U$ be an oriented open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(U)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TU)$ be smooth, and let $\mu_0>0$. Assume

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

with the sign convention of [[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. Define the Maxwell Hilbert tensor by the compact metric variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]],

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

Then

$$\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^{bc}j_c.$$

All fields and derivatives are smooth on $U$. In length-coordinate SI bookkeeping, assign $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; these are formal units and not observed values. Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]).

**(a) Characterization of Killing fields.** For every smooth vector field
$\xi$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]), with
$\xi_b=g_{bc}\xi^c$ the lowered field,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0 .$$

**(b) Contraction along geodesics.** If $\xi$ is a Killing field and
$\gamma:I\to M$ is a geodesic with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its affine parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]), then $t\mapsto
g_{\gamma(t)}(\xi_{\gamma(t)},\gamma'(t))$ is constant on $I$.

**(c) Conserved current.** Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $T$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $U$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $\xi$ be a Killing field on $U$. Then
$J^{a}:=T^{ab}\xi_b$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ with
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$; consequently the flux balance of
[[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] clause (b) applies to $J$
on every smooth singular $4$-chain contained in $U$.

**(d) On-shell conservation of the Hilbert tensor.** Let $c>0$, let
$S:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be a model action with Hilbert stress-energy tensor
$T$ at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]). For the flow diffeomorphisms $F$
below, suppose the configuration set $\mathcal X$ carries specified maps
$P_F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X$ with $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$; write
$F^*\varphi:=P_F(\varphi)$. For geometric matter fields these are the
model's pullbacks; no pullback operation on an arbitrary set is implicit.
For **every** smooth compactly supported vector field $\xi$, its flow
$\Phi_v$ is global
([[def-complete-vector-field]], [[def-local-and-global-flow]]); this holds for
every compactly supported smooth field, using the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] through
[[thm-compactly-supported-vector-fields-are-complete]]. Write
$G(u,v):=S(\Phi_v^*g,\Phi_u^*\varphi)$ for the simultaneous pullback by the
flow (this presupposes that the pairs lie in $\mathcal D$, which is part of the
hypotheses below). Suppose (H1)–(H4) hold for **every** such $\xi$ (with
its own $G$ and parameter neighborhood):

- **(H1)** the map $G$ is defined on a neighborhood of $(0,0)$ in
  $\mathbb R^2$ and is differentiable at $(0,0)$;
- **(H2)** $\partial_uG(0,0)=0$ (the matter configuration $\varphi$ satisfies
  its model equations in this direction);
- **(H3)** $\partial_vG(0,0)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_MT_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g$,
  where $q^{ab}:=\partial_v(\Phi_v^*g)^{ab}|_{v=0}$ (the metric variation is
  represented by the Hilbert tensor);
- **(H4)** $G(s,s)=S(g,\varphi)$ whenever $(s,s)$ lies in that neighborhood
